summary: Describes an LDAP extended operation to cancel an outstanding operation. Unlike the normal Abandon operation, it returns a response telling the client the outcome, like the Abandon operation in X.511 DAP.

eli5.summary: If you ask a librarian for a book and change your mind, this lets you say, "Never mind," and get a reply that confirms it.

questions: difference between ldap abandon and cancel
subtitle: An LDAP extended operation that cancels a running request and tells the client how the cancel turned out.

tldr.problem: The LDAP Abandon operation has no response, so a client that abandons a request never learns whether the abandon worked.
tldr.mechanism: The Cancel extended operation, identified by OID 1.3.6.1.1.8, names the message ID of the outstanding operation and gets a response. On success the cancelled operation fails with a canceled result code.
tldr.outcome: Clients get a clear outcome (success, noSuchOperation, tooLate or cannotCancel) and SHOULD use Cancel instead of Abandon when they need one.

facts.label: Not cancelable
facts.value: Abandon, Bind, Start TLS, Unbind, Cancel

today: RFC 3909 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Cancel Exists
sections.content:
LDAP (the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) already has an Abandon operation that clients can use to stop other operations. Abandon has no response, and it does not require a response from the abandoned operation. The client therefore gets no clear indication of the outcome.

The X.511 Directory Access Protocol (DAP) has an Abandon operation that does have a response, and it requires the abandoned operation to return a response saying it was cancelled. The LDAP Cancel operation is modeled after that DAP Abandon.

The RFC says Cancel SHOULD be used instead of Abandon when the client needs an indication of the outcome. It may be used to cancel both interrogation (read) and update operations.
sections.eli5: Telling a friend "never mind" and walking away leaves you unsure whether they heard you. Cancel is like asking them to wave back so you know.

sections.title: The Cancel Request and Response
sections.content:
Cancel is an LDAP extended operation (RFC 2251, Section 4.12) identified by the object identifier 1.3.6.1.1.8. The request is an ExtendedRequest whose requestName is that OID and whose requestValue holds a BER-encoded cancelRequestValue.

That value is a SEQUENCE with a single field, cancelID, which is the message ID of the operation to cancel. The response is an ExtendedResponse in which the responseName and response fields are absent, so the outcome is carried in the result code alone.
sections.eli5: The request is a note that says "please stop job number 7". The reply is a short note back saying yes or no.

sections.title: How Cancel Behaves
sections.content:
Cancel asks the server to cancel an outstanding operation issued within the same session. The Cancel request has its own, distinct message ID, and its cancelID carries the ID of the target. Clients SHOULD NOT request the cancelation of an operation multiple times.

If the server is willing and able to cancel, it SHALL return a Cancel response with a success result code, and the cancelled operation SHALL fail with the canceled result code. Otherwise the Cancel response SHALL have a non-success result code and SHALL NOT affect the outstanding operation, if it exists.

Servers SHOULD advertise support by listing 1.3.6.1.1.8 in the supportedExtension attribute of the root DSE. A server MAY advertise it only to clients that are authorized to use it.
sections.eli5: If the helper can stop the job, they say "done" and the job is marked as stopped. If they cannot, the job just carries on as if you never asked.

sections.title: Result Codes and What Cannot Be Cancelled
sections.content:
Implementations SHALL recognize four additional result codes: canceled (118), noSuchOperation (119), tooLate (120) and cannotCancel (121).

  • protocolError comes back if the server cannot parse the request value, or it is absent.
  • noSuchOperation means the server has no knowledge of the named operation.
  • tooLate means it is too late. For example, a modify that has already committed updates to the data store.
  • cannotCancel means the operation does not support cancelation, or the cancel could not be performed.

Some classes of operation are not cancelable: those with no response, those that create, alter or destroy authentication or authorization associations, those that establish, alter or tear down security services, and those that abandon or cancel other operations. Specifically, Abandon, Bind, Start TLS, Unbind and Cancel cannot be cancelled. The Cancel operation also cannot be abandoned.
sections.eli5: You cannot cancel a job that is already finished, one the helper never heard of, or special jobs like logging in. Each "no" comes with its own reason.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Cancel is meant to let a user cancel operations they previously issued during the current LDAP association. When something like the Proxy Authorization Control is in use, different outstanding operations may be processed under different associations, so servers MUST NOT allow a user to cancel an operation belonging to another user.

Some operations should not be cancelable for security reasons. Bind and Start TLS are excluded to avoid adding complexity to authentication, authorization and security layer semantics. Designers of future extended operations and controls are told to disallow abandonment and cancelation when appropriate.
sections.eli5: You can only cancel your own jobs, never someone else's. Login jobs cannot be cancelled either, to keep things safe.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The IANA registered three things upon Standards Action. First, the LDAP Object Identifier 1.3.6.1.1.8 for the Cancel operation. Second, an LDAP Protocol Mechanism entry for the same OID, with usage "Extended Operation". Third, the four result codes: canceled (118), noSuchOperation (119), tooLate (120) and cannotCancel (121).
sections.eli5: The new number for Cancel and the four new answer codes were written down in an official list so nobody else reuses them.

items.label: canceled
items.desc: The cancelled operation fails with this code.

items.label: noSuchOperation
items.desc: The server has no knowledge of the named operation.

items.label: tooLate
items.desc: It is too late to cancel the operation.

items.label: cannotCancel
items.desc: The operation is not cancelable or the cancel could not be done.
